thread:
incident-bot: Paging: service:redwood-inference-frontend p99 latency > 5s (streaming) — alerts escalated to on-call (maya).

maya: acked — looking. seeing p95 ~ 700ms, p99 ~ 6.2s across multiple pods. streaming stalls on model-route: r-bert-quant-v2.

alex: i can repro a tail spike on a few requests that hit GPU pool-42. logs show repeated `NVML ECC corrected` and thermal warnings from the node.

maya: pinging k8s-bot to check node health and pod distribution.

k8s-bot: Node gpu-node-42: NotReady -> Ready flapping (3x in 15m). Evicted pods: 12. GPU metrics: memory_util 86%, temp_peak 92C, ECC_CORRECTABLE_COUNT increased by 420 over 20m.

jamal: ugh. that ECC count jump + temp 92C explains streaming stalls — KV cache misses + kernel retries. are we seeing degraded throughput or stalls only?

alex: both. throughput dips then long tail while KV warmup finishes. also a couple of `cuCtxLock` timeouts in the runtime logs. snippet:

```
2026-03-15T03:12:04Z runtime ERROR kernel_launch_timeout pid=4123 gpu=gpu-node-42
2026-03-15T03:12:06Z hw WARN NVML: ECC correctable threshold reached: 420 events
2026-03-15T03:12:09Z runtime WARN streaming stall detected seq=0..512 elapsed=4.8s
```

maya: immediate plan: 1) drain gpu-node-42 from serving pool 2) route traffic off to warm spare pool-11 (lower capacity) with model-fallback rules 3) open ticket with HW team and vendor for ECC/thermal. I'll start the drain now.

sre-lead: +1. set `max_inflight` down for the route temporarily, enable our model-variant fallback to `r-bert-quant-v1` for streaming endpoints to reduce GPU work. notify support for customer impact comms.

k8s-bot: cordon/gpu-node-42 -> OK. drain initiated: 12 pods will grace-period terminate. ETA ~90s.

maya: executing route update: applying weight shift 100% pool-42 -> pool-11 over 30s; enabling fallback variant for streaming to v1.

support-sara: I'm drafting a short status for affected customers: "We detected an internal GPU issue causing higher-than-normal latency for streaming responses. We've mitigated by shifting traffic and enabling fallbacks. Some real-time requests may experience degraded p99 latency while we replace the node. We'll update within 1 hour." want approval to send?

maya: approved. include that we have no evidence of data loss, only latency.

jamal: re: metrics — can we toggle KV-prefetch aggressive caching on pool-11 to avoid warmup stalls? there are config knobs: `kv.cache.prefetch=true` and prefetch_size=64. would reduce tail at cost of memory.

sre-lead: do it for the fallback route only. Alex, can runtime accept those flags dynamically?

alex: yes, runtime accepts dynamic flags. applying to pool-11 now.

k8s-bot: pods drained from gpu-node-42. node now schedulable=false. no active serving pods.

hw-eng: from the node telemetry: repeated correctable ECC plus sustained high temp. likely fan degradation combined with a silicon area causing bursts of correctable errors under load. we recommend pulling out the card and running vendor diagnostics. opening HW ticket #HW-9921 and scheduling replacement.

ops-manager: good catch. estimate time to full remediation (replace card + validation) ~3-5 hours depending on vendor ETA. keep customers updated.

incident-bot: Update: SLO impact window started 2026-03-15T03:11Z. Current p99 across service: 1.8s (improved), streaming p99: 2.2s (improved). p95 steady ~600ms.

maya: thanks — looks like fallback + routing reduced observed p99 significantly. will continue monitoring telemetry for 30m then mark incident as mitigated if no regressions.

support-sara: sent customer notice to active customers affected by streaming endpoints. added note for status page post.

jamal: logging note for postmortem — include kernel backtraces for the `cuCtxLock` timeouts, NVML ECC spikes, and thermal telemetry. also capture request ids for the worst offender traces (I grabbed a sample set: reqs: [rQ-9933, rQ-9939, rQ-9961]).

alex: exporting runtime traces and perf counters to S3 -> s3://redwood-incidents/3321006789/traces.tar.gz. also saved node nvml logs to same bucket.

maya: handing to on-call followup: @sre-lead will own the postmortem and vendor coordination. I'm staying for 10m to help with rollbacks if needed.

sre-lead: taking. next actions: 1) confirm HW replacement schedule 2) run stress tests on replacement before rejoin 3) add eviction threshold tuning to avoid rapid node flapping 4) add alert to surface ECC correction-rate growth earlier.

incident-bot: Incident status -> MITIGATED (live routing + fallbacks). Impact: Elevated p99 for ~14m, some streaming stalls observed; no data loss.

ops-manager: excellent. add follow-up action to evaluate thermals across similar hosts — we should proactively check pool-42 sibling nodes. assign to hw-eng.

hw-eng: noted. we'll run parallel NVML sweeps and schedule any cards with rising ECC_correctable >100 in 24h for preemptive bench.

maya: closing timeline note. if any regressions ping me immediately. :thumbsup:

support-sara: will post final status page update once replacement confirmed.

sre-lead: will open postmortem doc and invite relevant owners.

incident-bot: thread closed by maya at 2026-03-15T04:13:09Z.
